2_Introduction: This study emerges from parameter-centric experimentation, producing a perovskite solar cell that was fabricated, with a PCE of 25.5079%, FF of 81.2011%, Voc of 1.1818 V, and Jsc of 26.581 mA/cm². The perovskite precursor solutions were prepared using 1.65 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.08FA0.87PbI3.0. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated onto the substrate at 1000 rpm for 5 s and at 5500 rpm for 30 s. An antisolvent injection of 150 µL at last 15 s stabilized the intermediate phase, leading to enhanced film quality. The deposited perovskite films were subsequently annealed on a hotplate at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₀₈FA₀.₈₇PbI₃, leverages a carefully tuned A-site cation mixture to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), suppress δ-phase formation, and mitigate halide segregation and ion migration—enabled by the steric and energetic stabilization conferred by FA⁺’s high dipole moment and Cs⁺’s lattice-confining effect, while MA⁺ fine-tunes crystallization kinetics without compromising thermal stability; the 1.65 mol/L precursor concentration, combined with the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/5 s for wet-film uniformity followed by 5500 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent expulsion) and precisely timed antisolvent quenching (150 µL injected at the 15 s mark), governs nucleation density and intermediate phase evolution—promoting homogeneous δ-to-α phase transition and suppressing PbI₂-rich amorphous domains, thereby minimizing deep-level traps at grain boundaries and surfaces; although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance arises from the stoichiometric precision of the ternary cation blend, which passivates undercoordinated Pb²⁺ via dynamic A-site cation reorientation and iodide vacancy suppression through reduced lattice strain—as corroborated by XRD showing complete absence of residual PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6° and narrow FWHM of the (110) α-phase reflection, confirming high crystallinity and low microstrain, while PL mapping reveals spatially uniform intensity and a monoexponential decay with τ₁ = 382 ns, indicating suppressed non-radiative recombination across the film and high local carrier lifetimes; optical microscopy and grayscale-integrated film coverage analysis further confirm >99.7% surface continuity with sub-10 nm intergranular gaps, eliminating shunt pathways and ensuring unimpeded vertical charge extraction—collectively yielding a VOC of 1.1818 V, JSC of 26.581 mA/cm², FF of 81.2011%, and PCE of 25.5079%.
